name: button
title: Button
purpose: An action the reader takes on the current view.
whenToUse: To start, save, confirm or cancel something on the current view.
whenNotToUse: To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
For an action repeated on every row of a list. Give that one secondary or quiet emphasis, never primary.
As a second primary action in the same view. A view has one.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Any action that is not the main one. A tonal fill a step from the page and from a raised card, with a faint border that turns strong on hover; unavailable, it loses the fill.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The one main action of a view, dialog or popover.

variants.name: quiet
variants.use: A minor action that should not draw the eye, such as Cancel or View log.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: An action that deletes or cannot be undone. The label names what is lost.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. Use it unless the button sits in a dense row.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: Drawn 32px tall for dense rows and toolbars. Its pointer target is still 44px.

accessibility: Use a button element, with type="button" unless it submits a form.
The label is a verb and what it acts on, such as Start task. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
Set the disabled attribute when the action is unavailable. A disabled button leaves the tab order.
Use aria-disabled="true" instead only when the button must stay focusable so its reason can be read. The app then ignores presses.
Set aria-busy="true" while the action runs, change the label to say what is happening, and ignore further presses.
Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.
